data.cultural_impact: The name Ramona gained popularity in the western world due to the eponymous novel 'Ramona' by Helen Hunt Jackson published in 1884. This novel portrayed the life of a half-Mexican, half-white girl growing up in California during the late 19th century. The name Ramona became a symbol of the multicultural heritage of the American West and its rich diversity.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, the name Ramona is linked to the figure of Mary, the Mother of Jesus, as the name Ramona is derived from Ram, a name used for Jesus in the Indian subcontinent. Ram is believed to be a vulnerable and compassionate form of God, and the name Ramona, meaning 'little one who is gentle', reflects the gentleness and loving nature of the Mother of God. It is a reminder of the divine presence and gentle guidance in our lives.

historical_references.reference: The name Ramona has been used throughout Christian history by saints, scholars, and faithful believers who exemplified its meaning.

modern_usage.modern_context: Ramona is a popular name in the US, particularly among Hispanics. It originated from the Spanish name 'Ramona de Tres Patas', which means 'Ramona of the Three Legs'. The name gained popularity in the US through the novel 'Ramona' by Helen Hunt Jackson, published in 1884.

name_in_real_life.story: Ruth Ramona from London, United Kingdom embodies the meaning of Ramona - "Little one who is gentle". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Ramona, derived from the Spanish name Ramona de la Cruz, holds symbolism of strength and resilience. It is believed that the name was given to a girl born from the sorrows of her mother, who suffered a great loss and found solace in the name that means "little one who is beloved and sorrowful."
